business_problem: ZF needed a database architecture that could handle massive real-time fleet telemetry for its SCALAR orchestration platform while supporting cloud migration, multi-cloud ambitions, and a simpler operating model for development teams.
solution_summary: ZF rebuilt the data foundation behind its SCALAR orchestration platform on MongoDB Atlas so it could ingest fleet telemetry in real time, unify current and historical vehicle state, and keep a simple operating model as volumes climbed. Atlas serves as the secure multi-cloud database layer for SaaS microservices that process driver-console traffic, route-optimization events, and technical-health data from more than 300,000 connected vehicles. MongoDB Time Series collections store current, historical, and subscription-oriented metrics, while Atlas Online Archive moves older data to cold storage without splitting query access across different systems. Atlas Charts publishes billing and cost insights to downstream product teams, and Atlas Search helps users find documentation across more than 30 databases. ZF also shards data horizontally across clusters and automates provisioning so developers can focus on new orchestration features instead of database administration.

data_flow: Vehicle and driver-console events stream into MongoDB Atlas, where time-series collections retain current and historical metrics; recent data stays hot for fast queries, older data moves to Atlas Online Archive, and Atlas Charts and Atlas Search surface billing insights and searchable operational information to internal and customer-facing workflows.
business_outcome: ZF can give customers faster, more proactive fleet orchestration while developers gain a scalable, cost-effective platform that is ready for future multi-cloud growth and new logistics services.
